extractions.value: Patient presented with pseudohemidystonia in a strict hemi-distribution, initially misdiagnosed as psychogenic dystonia. Spinal MRI showed lateral disc herniation at C6-C7 with left C7 root compression, presumably resulting from prolonged and fixed neck posture. FDG-PET showed normal metabolism in basal ganglia bilaterally.
extractions.quote: When facing a patient with hemidystonia, contralateral basal ganglia or thalamic structural lesion should be thought of first. This was excluded in our case. Other considerations, particularly in the presence of painful fixed dystonic posturing, are psychogenic dystonia and pseudodystonia... Some patients with fixed dystonic postures of the limb(s) or hemi-body (and in the absence of structural brain lesion) may be misdiagnosed as psychogenic if SPS is not considered in the differential diagnosis
